name: Citizenship by Birth and Descent

requirements.blocker_text: Born in Pakistan after the Act's commencement -- automatic citizenship by birth, except where the father held diplomatic immunity and was not a Pakistani citizen, or the birth occurred in enemy-occupied territory during wartime.

Parent held Pakistani citizenship (otherwise than by descent) at the time of the applicant's birth outside Pakistan; since an amendment effective 18 April 2000, citizenship transmits equally through a Pakistani mother or father.
Where the transmitting parent is themself a citizen by descent only, the applicant's birth must be registered at a Pakistani Consulate or Mission.
requirements.fix_path: Register the birth at a Pakistani Consulate or Mission.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT (academic global citizenship law database, EUI) -- Pakistan Citizenship Act 1951: Section 4 (birth in Pakistan, with diplomatic-immunity and enemy-occupation exceptions) and Section 5 (descent, extended to children of Pakistani mothers effective 18 April 2000, with consular registration required where the transmitting parent is themself a citizen by descent)

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Pakistan). STATUS: DRAFT -- unlike pk_citizenship_naturalisation.json and pk_citizenship_by_marriage.json, the government's own DGI&P citizenship page did not detail Sections 4 (birth) and 5 (descent) beyond naming them and noting the 2000 amendment on maternal transmission; the operative text used here is the GLOBALCIT (European University Institute) academic-hosted consolidated translation, tier-2 under this dataset's convention. GOOD NEWS FLAGGED EXPLICITLY: unlike several other countries built in this dataset (Nigeria's citizenship-by-marriage, Sudan's citizenship-by-marriage and by-descent, both restricted to one parental line historically), Pakistan's descent citizenship has been GENDER-NEUTRAL since the 18 April 2000 amendment -- both a Pakistani mother and a Pakistani father transmit citizenship on the same terms. This is a genuine positive finding, not an assumption.
